item.title: McIlroy to defend Irish Open title
item.description: Rory McIlroy has confirmed that he'll defend his Irish Open golf title in September. The Masters champion will tee it up at Trump International in Clare, where US President Donald Trump could be in attendance. McIlroy won his second Irish Open at the K Club last year. Advertisement

item.title: New dissent rules to come into effect for National League finals
item.description: Hurling's new dissent rules will come into effect for the upcoming National League finals. A motion was strongly backed at Congress to introduce a 30-metre penalty for arguing with officials. The GAA's director general Tom Ryan says they had considered bringing in the rule sooner, but he feels a 28-day period was needed to avoid 'short circuiting the process'. Advertisement

item.title: Coleman should be available for World Cup qualifier against Czech Republic
item.description: Seamus Coleman should be available for the Republic of Ireland's World Cup qualifier against the Czech Republic later this month. Everton boss David Coleman says the veteran defender picked up a knock in training last week, but it's not too serious. Evan Ferguson is likely to miss the game in Prague with an ankle issue, with Josh Cullen already ruled out with a knee injury. item.title: Wales rule out fly-half for trip to Ireland
item.description: Wales have ruled out fly-half Sam Costelow for Friday's trip to Ireland in the Six Nations. The Scarlets number 10 suffered an ankle injury in Wales' loss to Scotland nine days ago. He'll be replaced by Jarrod Evans or Dan Edwards, with the team set to be named on Wednesday afternoon. Advertisement

item.title: El Fabiolo eases to victory in QuinnBet Hurdle
item.description: El Fabiolo has eased to victory in the QuinnBet Hurdle at Leopardstown. Willie Mullins' four-time Grade One winner had 21-lengths to spare over the field under the ride of Paul Townend. The jockey says it's possible that El Fabiolo could now go back over fences again. item.title: Kerry Mountain Rescue Team appeal for hillwalkers to take simple safety precautions
item.description: Following a recent increase in call-outs for Kerry Mountain Rescue Team, they are appealing for hillwalkers in the county to take some simple safety measures. PRO of KMRT, Robert Fell says there have been seven call-outs since January, luckily all for minor injuries. These rescues took around 170 volunteer hours, but the team expects to be even busier during the summer. item.title: Kerry Co-Operative Creameries board suspending proposed 2026 share-up collection
item.description: The board of Kerry Co-Operative Creameries has decided to suspend the proposed 2026 share-up collection. The share-up, which was due to commence in April, would have required Kerry Dairy Ireland milk suppliers to contribute 1 cent per litre on milk supplied, until a total of 5 cents per litre was reached. item.title: Gardaí believe same group of criminals behind Killarney and Tralee car thefts
item.description: Gardaí in Kerry believe a group of criminals is behind thefts and attempted thefts of cars in multiple parts of the county last week. The incidents happened last week in Tralee and Killarney. Gardaí say two cars were taken from separate addresses in Killarney in the early hours of last Tuesday, 24th February. item.title: West Kerry final fixed for Sunday in Lispole
item.description: The West Kerry Football League final sponsored by Lee Strand has been fixed for Sunday in Lispole. An Ghaeltacht and Annascaul are to face off from 2. Advertisement

item.title: Ireland narrow pitch for World Cup qualifier against France
item.description: Ireland head coach Carla Ward has confirmed that they've narrowed the pitch at Tallaght Stadium for tomorrow's World Cup qualifier against France. Ward says the pitch has been reduced to the minimum size allowed by FIFA as they look to deny space to the French team. The Ireland boss says Hayley Nolan is a doubt for the game as she continues to recover from injuries to her calf and ankle. Advertisement
